title: Britain’s William and Kate ride e-rickshaw to meet climate prize finalists in Mumbai
html:
The Prince and Princess of Wales in an electric tuk-tuk during a royal visit for the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai on Nov 17.

PHOTO: REUTERS

MUMBAI – Britain’s Prince William drove his wife Kate Middleton in an electric auto-rickshaw in Mumbai on Nov 17, to a meeting with the finalists of a climate change award that they will announce later in the day.

The royal couple are in Mumbai, India’s financial capital, on a three-day visit centred around the Earthshot Prize, which aims to find solutions to climate change, and awards five winners £1 million (S$1.7 million) each to scale up their project.

The trip, which will conclude with a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Nov 18, marks the Princess of Wales’ most high-profile overseas visit since undergoing treatment for cancer in 2024.

On Nov 17, William rode an electric-powered auto-rickshaw to a waterfront overlooking the Bandra-Worli Sea Link bridge, which spans the Arabian Sea in Mumbai, with Kate sitting at the back, as they arrived to meet the finalists of the prize.

The couple shook hands with the finalists and posed for a picture, which was posted on their social media feeds.

“India is home to more Earthshot Prize Winners and Finalists than any other country,” the couple said in the caption accompanying the picture on Instagram.

“The Earthshot Prize is the global environmental prize finding and scaling solutions to repair the planet.”

Kate, 44, underwent preventative chemotherapy for an unspecified form of cancer, after which she significantly reduced her official workload.

Now in remission, she has gradually increased her public appearances, but had not joined William on previous foreign trips.

Her only significant overseas visit since 2024 was in May, when she travelled alone to Italy for two days as part of her work focusing on early childhood development. REUTERS
summary: It is the Princess of Wales’ most high-profile overseas visit since undergoing treatment for cancer in 2024.
